record.title: Brazil Pacaraima judicial suspension of Venezuelan migrant entry August 2018
record.movement: Venezuelan migrants seeking formal admission to Brazil; no demonstrated general goods prohibition.
record.exceptions: AFP explicitly reports Brazilians and other nationalities continued normally; Venezuelan departures permitted. Goods treatment not established.
record.imposing_authority: Brazilian Federal Police implementing lower-court injunction
record.enforcement: PF confirms implementing category-specific administrative admission suspension August6 and lifting it August7; its press note denies closure of the whole frontier.
record.consequences: UNHCR indexed field account reports210 people unable to finalize immigration procedures; no deportations or pushbacks in that account.
record.status_observation: Evidence dated in cited sources; no assumption of present status.
record.official_rationale: Lower-court restriction sought to condition further migrant entry on redistribution of Venezuelans already in Roraima.
record.uncertainty: Appellate reversal of a lower-court injunction; do not confuse this with a separate Supreme Court denial of the state government’s closure request. Informal paths remained permeable. PF denial concerns whole-border closure, not its admitted Venezuelan-entry prohibition. Press-note reprint is the PF lineage, not independent observation. Round14: UNHCR field observations qualify implementation, while its legal-summary attribution to a Supreme Court reversal conflicts with primary TRF1 chronology. UNHCR direct retrieval failed; substantial indexed text only. AFP onset headline date and dateline differ, but event explicitly Monday August6.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated actual reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. Contemporary report describes approximately 15 hours; police confirmed reopening around 10:00 August 7.
